title: The Loom That Clicked at Midnight

pages.text: Ablah spent the holidays with her uncle in Bonwire, a town famous for kente cloth. By day, the workshop clicked and clacked with looms and bright threads. By night, it was silent. Or it was supposed to be.
sentences: Ablah spent the holidays with her uncle in Bonwire, a town famous for kente cloth.
By day, the workshop clicked and clacked with looms and bright threads.
By night, it was silent.
Or it was supposed to be.
pages.alt: A busy kente weaving workshop by day with colourful threads and wooden looms.

pages.text: At midnight, Ablah woke to a sound: click… clack… click… clack. It came from the workshop. Her cousin Yoofi, awake too, whispered, “That is the old loom. Nobody has used it for years.” Ablah picked up her torch. “We must tell Nana Frempong.”
sentences: At midnight, Ablah woke to a sound: click… clack… click… clack.
It came from the workshop.
Her cousin Yoofi, awake too, whispered, “That is the old loom.
Nobody has used it for years.” Ablah picked up her torch.
“We must tell Nana Frempong.”
pages.alt: Two children in a dark bedroom listen to faint clicking from the weaving shed.

pages.text: They found the master weaver, Nana Frempong, already awake and sitting on his stool. “I heard it too,” he said calmly. “Stay behind me. We will look from the door.” They crept to the shed and peered in. Nobody was there, but the old loom’s shuttle was gliding back and forth by itself.
sentences: They found the master weaver, Nana Frempong, already awake and sitting on his stool.
“I heard it too,” he said calmly.
“Stay behind me.
We will look from the door.” They crept to the shed and peered in.
Nobody was there, but the old loom’s shuttle was gliding back and forth by itself.
pages.alt: An old weaver and two children look into a dark workshop where a loom moves on its own.

pages.text: Yoofi shivered. “A spirit?” Nana Frempong stepped closer, careful and slow. “This loom is old,” he said. “Some say the weavers before us still work here. But a weaver also checks the loom.” He sniffed the air. “Do you smell something?” Ablah sniffed. There was a faint smell of something hot.
sentences: Yoofi shivered.
“A spirit?” Nana Frempong stepped closer, careful and slow.
“This loom is old,” he said.
“Some say the weavers before us still work here.
But a weaver also checks the loom.” He sniffed the air.
“Do you smell something?” Ablah sniffed.
There was a faint smell of something hot.
pages.alt: The weaver sniffs the air near the loom while the children watch nervously.

pages.text: Ablah shone her torch along the wall behind the loom. A wire had split. A tiny blue spark jumped from it, again and again, and a scrap of thread nearby was beginning to glow. “An electrical fault!” she gasped. “Sparks near thread, and thread burns!” The “clicking” was the spark making the old loom’s metal parts jump.
sentences: Ablah shone her torch along the wall behind the loom.
A wire had split.
A tiny blue spark jumped from it, again and again, and a scrap of thread nearby was beginning to glow.
“An electrical fault!” she gasped.
“Sparks near thread, and thread burns!” The “clicking” was the spark making the old loom’s metal parts jump.
pages.alt: A torch lights a sparking wire near hanging threads.

pages.text: Nana Frempong acted at once. “Out! Everyone out!” “Yoofi, blow your whistle! Ablah, wake the neighbours!” The weavers’ houses were close together, and cloth and thread burn quickly. Yoofi blew until his face was red. Ablah ran from door to door. Nobody stayed to fight a fire in a room full of thread.
sentences: Nana Frempong acted at once.
“Out!
Everyone out!” “Yoofi, blow your whistle!
Ablah, wake the neighbours!” The weavers’ houses were close together, and cloth and thread burn quickly.
Yoofi blew until his face was red.
Ablah ran from door to door.
Nobody stayed to fight a fire in a room full of thread.
pages.alt: A boy blows a whistle and a girl knocks on neighbours’ doors in the night.

pages.text: Nana Frempong called the emergency number from the street. Within minutes, neighbours stood safely across the road. When the fire service arrived, they cut the power at the main switch and checked the shed. The scrap of thread was smoking, but the workshop was saved. “You acted fast and stayed safe,” said the officer.
sentences: Nana Frempong called the emergency number from the street.

When the fire service arrived, they cut the power at the main switch and checked the shed.
The scrap of thread was smoking, but the workshop was saved.
“You acted fast and stayed safe,” said the officer.
pages.alt: Neighbours stand in the street as firefighters with a torch check the shed.

pages.text: In the morning, Nana Frempong laid a small strip of kente on Ablah’s hands. “You are a weaver of brave choices,” he said. As the sun rose, Ablah noticed that the old loom’s newest thread, one nobody remembered placing, was gold and shone like a tiny sunrise. “Science found the spark,” she smiled. “But who put that thread there?” The end.

pages.alt: A girl holds a strip of kente cloth in the sunrise beside the old loom with one shining golden thread.

activities.question: What did Ablah find behind the loom?
Why did everyone leave instead of trying to put out the fire themselves?
